$comment: Game-type registry. The type axis (interaction model) is ORTHOGONAL to the blueprint axis (small/medium/large = scale). Adding a type means adding an entry here plus a subsection in references/design/13-Types.md — never editing SKILL.md's pipeline. Schema: ./type-registry.schema.json

axis.rationale: In the 329-file corpus only 17 files (5.2%) contain update() tick logic and 53.5% are pure-formula layers. Whether the player acts or not decides the whole component-generation path, so it is the strongest separating axis. Scale (blueprint) stays exactly as it is: Q2 -> blueprints.<key>, 1:1, 'do not mix blueprints' unchanged.

corpus.source: E:/Idle-Skill/archive/data/tmt_index.json + direct source regex over E:/Idle-Skill/The-Modding-Tree-eg/
caveats: The corpus unit is a FILE, not a game: 171/329 are author_game__part.js fragments and 193/297 carry a single layer. Corpus shares are therefore a fallback prior only — never allowed to override stated user intent (weight 0.15, see routing.weights).

The index's `minified` flag is INVERTED (true = 68.6 bytes/line, median 691 lines; false = 689.8 bytes/line, median 29 lines). All genuine one-line vendor blobs are flagged false. Never stratify by it.
The index reports grids=0 because it only looked for addGrid(). Grids exist in 22 files as the declarative key `grid: {`; addGrid() has 0 call sites corpus-wide.

notes: `explicit` is a floor, not an addition: when the user names a type outright, that type's score is raised to at least 0.75 and no other signal can lower it.

The passive-prestige signal is ABSENCE-based: passive wins when no action-bearing verb matches AND the request reads as incremental/idle. Any action verb hit suppresses it, so 'idle mining' resolves to passive, not tick.

active-click|active-tick.zh: 核心操作是离散点击(每次一下),还是持续进度(看着进度条走完)?
active-click|active-tick.en: Is the core action discrete clicks (one tap at a time), or continuous progress (watching a bar fill)?

active-click|passive-prestige.zh: 点击是核心玩法,还是偶尔的加速手段?
active-click|passive-prestige.en: Is clicking the core of the game, or an occasional accelerator?

active-tick|passive-prestige.zh: 进度条只是显示状态,还是玩家真正在推的进度?
active-tick|passive-prestige.en: Does the bar just display state, or is it progress the player is actually pushing?

board-minigame|*.zh: 需要二维棋盘/网格承载玩法,还是只要把升级排成网格?
board-minigame|*.en: Do you need a real 2D board/grid to hold the gameplay, or just upgrades laid out in a grid?

*|passive-prestige.zh: 你想要纯挂机体验,还是希望手上有事可做?
*|passive-prestige.en: Do you want a pure idle experience, or something to actively do?

evidence.note: references/design/09:438 — Mining is 2.7MB/59k lines; keep this sparing

score-attack.label: M2 分数攻击挑战枢纽
score-attack.contract: startData holds a maxpoints[] array; update() records the peak inside the challenge; challengeEffect() reads the peak

evidence.note: The engine has NO scoreAttack / maxScore / leaderboard API (0 corpus hits). M2 is a hand-rolled idiom, which is exactly why it depends on a tick.

score-attack.downgradeReason: M2 needs update() to record a peak. Without a tick or a sim layer the pattern cannot be generated correctly.

minigame.label: M3 风险收益小游戏
minigame.contract: a clickable group as pickable targets + style() state feedback + run state in startData
minigame.downgradeReason: M3 is built on clickables. Without them there is nothing to click.

board.label: 网格板玩法
board.contract: grid: { getStartData, rows, cols, getCanClick, getStyle, getUnlocked }; ids base-100

evidence.keyForm: declarative grid: { — addGrid() has 0 call sites corpus-wide

evidence.note: canComplete() is the corpus majority dialect; the goal:+rewardEffect shape the handbooks teach is the minority.

caps.label: 主题自然硬上限
caps.contract: capped currency uses type:"custom" + softcap(x, cap, 0); its ladder STOPS at the cap

signals: No action-bearing verb appears in the Q1 structure recap.
The request reads as incremental/idle (see keywords).
Q4 answered 'Mostly idle' or 'Balanced' with no action verb.
antiSignals: The theme's core verb is a direct player action (click / mine / chop / place).
The user explicitly asks for game feel or a minigame.

counterExamples.desc: Clickables exist but are only a garnish — 95% of the layers are still formula layers.
counterExamples.howToTell: If clickables < mainLayers * 0.2, still classify passive-prestige.

require: normal/static layers carry baseResource + baseAmount() + requires

acceptance.exemptRationale: Having no tick is the CORRECT shape for this type. Today D-NOUPDATE only guards games with >=4 main layers, so a 3-layer prestige chain is silently unchecked — exemption is what makes the type explicit.

failureModes.symptom: 数字爆炸 / 几分钟通关
failureModes.fix: Check the three causes in this order (SKILL.md:456).

active-click.name: 点击驱动

signals: Q4 = 'Mostly active' AND the recap verb is a discrete action.
The user explicitly asks for game feel / something to press.
antiSignals: The core action is continuous progress (mining / charging / growing) -> active-tick.
Clicking is only an accelerator (see counterExamples).

counterExamples.desc: Clickables as a garnish on a formula game.
counterExamples.howToTell: clickables < mainLayers * 0.2, or every clickable is a one-off 'get N' button rather than a repeated verb.

require: every clickable defines canClick() and onClick()
clickable state is initialised in startData (handbook 10 §6)
clickable state is a number or a string only (hard rule 11)
forbid: an arrow-function onClick that uses this

process: Stage 4.2 generates the clickable group before the layer

acceptance.gapNote: T-CLICKABLE is new. Today the checker only COUNTS clickables (D-MECHQUOTA) and never checks one is usable.

failureModes.cause: onClick written as an arrow function using this

active-tick.name: tick 生产循环

signals: Q4 = 'Mostly active' AND the recap verb is a continuous quantity.
The core action is watching a bar fill (mining / charging / growing).
antiSignals: The bar only displays state — in the corpus only 12.3% of bar files define progress(), the rest are decorative HUD -> passive-prestige.

counterExamples.desc: Bars as pure HUD: every bar defines width/height but no progress().
counterExamples.howToTell: If no bar in the game defines progress(), the tick is not the core loop.

require: update() uses addPoints() and never assigns player[layer].points directly
every custom action-function is listed in doNotCallTheseFunctionsEveryTick
forbid: Decimal.pow with a large exponent inside the tick

process: Stage 4.2 followed by a tick-budget step

acceptance.gapNote: T-TICKREG is new and mandatory here: M-DNC today (SC:460) only checks the declaration exists, never that it lists the hooks the game actually defines.

failureModes.fix: move the computation into gainMult / passiveGeneration

signals: The gameplay needs a 2D board or matrix.
antiSignals: You only want upgrades laid out in a 5x5 grid — that is the `grid` LAYOUT on upgrades, not a grid COMPONENT.

counterExamples.desc: Upgrades arranged in a grid via addGrid on the layer, with no grid component.
counterExamples.howToTell: No `grid: {` key inside a layer's component block.

require: ids follow the base-100 scheme (hard rule 10)

acceptance.gapNote: T-GRID is new and is the single biggest checker gap: 22 real files use grid and the checker covers none of it.

fallback.rationale: 53.5% of the corpus is pure-formula. It is the cheapest type to verify and its failure modes are the most predictable. Falling back to passive is safer than falling back to an interaction type that would force components the user never asked for.

mixedPolicy.rationale: The skill already caps this: at most ONE type:"none" core-loop layer per game (SKILL.md:99; P15 warns Mining is 2.7MB/59k lines).
mixedPolicy.onHardDependencyMissing: downgrade the modifier, and record the downgrade in brief §10 with the reason — never drop it silently.
mixedPolicy.unknownType: Ask once; if the user cannot name one, fall back and record 'unrecognised, defaulted' in brief §10.
